name: Counters (They Count Everything)
description:
Written and recorded in 2196 by Miriam Achebe-Søren under the name the Gray Zone-born pseudonym 'Dust Mouth,' Counters is a six-minute anti-surveillance anthem built over a grinding, repetitive rhythmic structure deliberately designed to feel like being processed — like being counted. The lyrics are a catalog of what the corporate surveillance apparatus measures: steps taken, calories consumed, BCI idle-time, blink rate, social contact hours, emotional valence scores, productivity indices, augmentation maintenance compliance. Each verse adds more items to the list, the arrangement growing more claustrophobic, until the final chorus strips everything back to a single repeated line — 'they count everything except what it costs you' — delivered over near-silence.

The song was banned by Vantablack Media's content compliance division within three weeks of its pirate-feed release, on grounds that it 'constitutes incitement to non-compliance with lawful data collection practices.' The ban made it immediately ubiquitous. It is estimated to be the most-shared pirate feed track in GLMZ history. Dust Mouth's identity as Achebe-Søren was leaked in 2201; she has since performed under her real name but the pseudonym is still used to distribute the song.
creator: Miriam Achebe-Søren (as Dust Mouth)
audience: the Gray Zone residents, civil liberties activists, anti-corporate organizers, underground journalists, anyone who has been flagged by corporate compliance systems, Tier 2 workers resentful of workplace monitoring
cultural_impact: Counters is arguably the most politically consequential song released in GLMZ in the last thirty years. Its ban transformed it from a protest song into a symbol of protest itself — listening to it is an act of defiance, and the pirate feeds that distribute it are among the most actively hunted by Vantablack Media's content enforcement teams. The song has been played at every major labor action since 2198 and its final line has been stenciled onto walls across the Gray Zone and the Circuit. Miriam Achebe-Søren has been arrested twice; both times the charges were eventually dropped amid significant public pressure.
known_fans: the Gray Zone residents and activists
story_hooks: Vantablack Media's enforcement division has identified the pirate feed node responsible for the most recent mass distribution of Counters — it is located in a children's community center in the Gray Zone, and the operator is a retired teacher.
A Tier 4 corporate compliance officer has Counters on a private data chip they carry everywhere and has never told anyone — until a search of their belongings turns it up.

Someone releases a version of Counters with the final line changed — 'they count everything, and so do we' — and it is unclear whether this is a radical evolution of the song or a corporate co-option attempt.
